title: Criminal Code Amendment (Prohibition of Full Face Coverings in Public Places) Bill 2017
short_title: Criminal Code Amendment (Prohibition of Full Face Coverings in Public Places) Bill 2017

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would prohibit full face coverings in public places within Commonwealth jurisdiction during specified terrorism threat declarations, and criminalise forcing others to wear them.
The minister would have to declare the prohibition when the national terrorism threat level is above Possible, covering Commonwealth places and Australian territories.
Exceptions would allow coverings for lawful work, entertainment, recreation, sport, genuine artistic purposes and protection, with the amendments starting the day after Royal Assent.
changes: Wearing a full face covering during an operative declaration would become an offence in covered public places.
Compelling an adult to wear an identity-concealing garment would become a separate offence.
Compelling a child to wear such a garment would also become an offence.
Ministerial threat declarations would not be subject to parliamentary disallowance.
summary.affected: People wearing face coverings in covered public places and adults or children compelled to wear them are affected.
